flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c4 with your knight is a blunder because it reveals an attack on the king and the pawn was undefended. A better move would have been moving your knight to e4 because you can likely fork the black c8-rook and the black b7-rook.
flags.critique: You just told me a 370-centipawn dump is a blunder *because* it discovers check and takes a hanging pawn — those are reasons it looks *good*. Concept `check` is winning the lecture over the actual mistake. Ne4+ does not fork c8 and b7; a knight on e4 hits c3/c5/d6/f6. If Nd6 is a later PV trick, say *then*, don't pin it on this move. Teach the d-file discovered check and why landing on c4 throws the win.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your f3-knight is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: The d-pawn is defended by the knight on c6. This is the Open Sicilian recapture, not a free pawn. `wins_material` plus 'undefended' on an equal recapture is a lie a 900 will believe, then hang the next one for real.

flags.quote: Moving your c4-bishop to b5 is the strongest move because it saves your b5-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is not on b5 until it lands there. You named the destination square as the thing being saved. It was hanging on c4 to ...d5; Bb5+ runs away *and* checks. Tell me that, not this Escher sentence.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: ...d5 is the Sicilian break: it hits e4, challenges the c4-bishop, and opens the center. My king is still on e8. `pawn_shield` and `king_safer` together are a coin-flip lecture. Teach the break or don't talk.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to g7 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: This is the Accelerated Dragon bishop. I played g6 to put it on the long diagonal, not to relatively pin b2 to a1. That pin does nothing this move. You buried the only idea worth learning under a geometry toy.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d7 with your king is the strongest move because the queen was undefended.
flags.critique: The king is the only legal recapture after Qxd7+. It is not winning a queen; it is completing a trade and parking the king in the center. Dumping `king_more_exposed` and `king_safer` on the same ply is you arguing with yourself.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c6 with your d4-knight is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn and you take the defender of the black queen.
flags.critique: The queen 'attack' on d7 is a well-defended pawn, not a tactic. Nc6 does not defend the queen on d8. Nxc6 is a structure choice (force ...bxc6) that also costs 41cp while you still call it strongest. Fake discovered attack plus fake removed-defender.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c6 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: White's queen defends c6. This is a recapture, not a free piece, and `wins_material` is wrong. The lesson is ...bxc6 vs ...Qxc6: extra center pawn and the b-file, at the cost of doubled c-pawns. You taught the opposite of structure.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on b5 with your d7-bishop is the strongest move because you fork the white queen and the white f1-rook and you take the defender of the white queen.
flags.critique: After Bxb5 the bishop *geometrically* eyes Qa4 and Rf1 — then White recaptures Qxb5+ and the 'fork' is gone. That is a trade, not a fork. 'Defender of the white queen' is the same removed-defender hallucination as Nxc6.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e3 with your knight is the strongest move because you take the defender of the white d1-rook.
flags.critique: Be3 does not defend Rd1. I took a bishop with a knight; the story is piece quality and the doubled e-pawns after fxe3. Stop inventing a defender for a rook on a different color complex.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Bc4 defends d5. Equal recapture, again sold as a hanging pawn and `wins_material`. The real choice is recapturing toward the center and opening the c-file. I am done trusting 'undefended.'

flags.quote: Moving your knight to d6 leaves your d1-rook overloaded. A better move would have been moving your d1-rook to d3.
flags.critique: Nd6 *looks* like a gorgeous fork of both rooks. The lesson is why that fork is fake: ...Rxc1 pins Rd1 to the king, and if you recapture, ...Kxd6; if you take b7, the back rank explodes. 'Overloaded' plus Rd3 with no because-clause is a shrug at a 500-centipawn swing.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c4 with your d-pawn puts it at risk of attack from the white c1-rook and knight. A better move would have been moving your b7-rook to c7 because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: My king is on d7. Capturing on c4 opens the d-file onto that king and allows Nxc4 *with check*. You talked about a hanging pawn like I dropped a coffee. 'Puts it at risk' doesn't even say which 'it.' The pin-on-c4 line is a sideshow next to king-in-the-center.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to f5 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on c3 with your bishop would be better because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the white a1-rook.
flags.critique: You *just* said Nd2 left c3 hanging to the bishop, then I missed Bxc3 — good catch — and immediately lied about why. The c3-pawn does not defend a1. Bxc3 *attacks* a1 from the long diagonal. Lichess calls this a blunder (180cp); you called it a mistake. At least name the hanging pawn without the defender fanfic.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty reasons, 26cp tagged strongest, and this is the Accelerated Dragon: g6 prepares Bg7. Zero teaching. If you have nothing, don't purr 'That's the one.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This *is* the Open Sicilian: I trade my c-pawn for White's d-pawn. You listed hanging, doubled pawns, backward pawn, and capture — a junk drawer. d4 is defended by Nf3. Teach the trade or admit you only noticed a capture.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to a4 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: The a7-to-a8 pin is wallpaper. Qa4 plus Bb5 is a battery on the pinned bishop on d7. Also 50cp loss called strongest. You keep picking the incidental pin and missing the one I actually need.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e3 with your f-pawn is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: Recapture. You even had `pawn_shield`, isolated, and backward in the reason pile — the f-pawn leaving the king — and still printed 'undefended knight.' Doubled e-pawns and a drafty king is the lesson. Tactical because-clauses ate it.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: e6 prepares ...d5 and blunts Bc4. The king is still in the center. 'Harder to attack' is the `king_safer` slot firing because a pawn moved near the king. Then I play ...d5 and you call *that* king safety too. Pattern, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d7 with your queen is the strongest move because it forces the king to respond.
flags.critique: That is the definition of check. We are trading queens and dragging the king to d7. 'Forces the king to respond' is a phrase-bank shrug. Also `hanging` on a queen the king is about to take.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: d4 in a Sicilian offers a pawn trade to open the position. I am not 'controlling more squares'; I am blowing the center open. Same three center-control sentences as e4 and Nf3. Opening theory vs Mad Libs.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-bishop to c4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Empty reasons. The bishop eyes f7 and the uncastled king. 'f1-bishop' plus 'That's the one.' is not coaching; it is a caption.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to e7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: 45cp, still 'strongest,' still no reason. Developing the knight, connecting, heading for f5. You had a development slot in the opening and then forgot pieces exist.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d7 is the strongest move because it gives your king better protection.
flags.critique: I am blocking a check and offering a queen trade. Same `king_safer` mush as Bd7, e6, and ...d5. If every legal reply to check is 'king protection,' the phrase means nothing.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on c1 with your c8-rook is the strongest move because you pin the rook to the king and you take the defender of the white d1-rook.
flags.critique: This is the shot that proves Nd6 was a fake fork. After ...Rxc1 the d1-rook is pinned, so recapture loses the knight to ...Kxd6 and Nxb7 walks into the back rank. 'Pin and removed defender' is the geometry without the punchline. I played the tactic; explain why it wins.

suggestions.title: Never justify a blunder with its benefits
suggestions.detail: select-insight sets explainPlayedAsBenefit when concept is check/capture, so a 371cp Nxc4+ becomes 'is a blunder because it reveals an attack on the king and the pawn was undefended.' If classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, force pickProblemReasons (or missed_improvement) and keep check/capture benefits off the because-clause. A 1200 hears 'you blundered by checking and taking' and stops listening.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures free pieces
suggestions.detail: wins_material plus move-copy's 'the X was undefended' (seeCp >= pieceValue - 50) fired on Nxd4, bxc6, cxd5, Kxd7, fxe3 — all equal recaptures, several clearly defended. Gate wins_material on net SEE after a full exchange, or drop it when the captured unit was just the opponent's previous capture. This single lie showed up more than any other in this game.

suggestions.title: Require the captured piece to actually guard the target
suggestions.detail: removed_defender claimed Nc6 defends the queen, Bb5 defends the queen, c3 defends a1, Be3 defends d1. detectRemovedDefender should require a legal attack from defender square to newlyHanging before the capture, and newlyHanging hanging after. Optionally demand SEE on the newly hanging unit. Incidental geometry is teaching anti-chess.

suggestions.title: Demote unused pins and recapture-forks
suggestions.detail: Bg7 'pins the pawn to the rook,' Qa4 pins a7 to a8, Bxb5 'forks' queen and rook that recapture immediately. Rank relative pins of unthreatened pawns and forks whose extra target is recaptured on the next legal reply below development/structure. pickBenefitReasons already ranks; add a usefulness gate (pinned unit attacked, or fork SEE). Learners notice when the named tactic isn't why anyone played the move.

suggestions.title: Name saved pieces from the square they fled
suggestions.detail: retreatedToSafety labels movedPiece at move.to, so Bb5+ 'saves your b5-bishop.' Describe from-square or piece type without the landing square ('saves your bishop from ...d5'). Same bug will tautologize every retreat. Cheap, high-visibility fix in ownedPhrase / saves_piece copy.

suggestions.title: Stop using king_safer as the pawn-move default
suggestions.detail: e6, ...d5, Bd7, Qd7 all got king-safety copy. Add a blocks_check / interposes reason from effects when the move ends a check, and a central-break tag when ...d5 (or d4) captures or attacks a center pawn. Gate king_safer in the opening unless castle or pawn shield actually changed. Four different ideas collapsed into one mushy sentence.

suggestions.title: Don't pin PV follow-ups on the suggested move
suggestions.detail: Ne4+ 'because you can likely fork' the two rooks — Ne4 attacks neither; Nd6 in the PV does. verifyLikelyTactics should require the suggested piece on its landing square to attack both fork targets, or templates should say 'then you can fork.' Empty suggestion becauses (Rd3, Re1) should pull one ranked benefit or stay silent, not a naked 'would have been.'

suggestions.title: Teach the named plan, not center Mad Libs
suggestions.detail: c5, d4, cxd4, g6, Bg7, ...d5 were all center_control / empty / fake pin. A tiny phase=opening plan table (flank-pawn vs d4, open-center trade, fianchetto, ...d5 break) as reason kinds feeding phrase-bank is deterministic and would have salvaged the first 16 plies. 'Strongest move' with 26–50cp loss should also drop to excellent/good per classification thresholds so the quip stops being 'That's the one' on every breath.

whatWorked: O-O: king shelter plus rook toward the center is actually the idea.
b3: correctly 'saves your pawn from capture' after ...Rb8 hit b2.
Rb7: defending a7 against Be3 is the right hanging-pawn read.
Rd1: pin of the d5-pawn to the king on the open file — real tactic, clear sentence.
Nd2: 'leaves your pawn hanging to the black bishop' is the c3/Bg7 story a learner can use.
Rac1: actually defends the hanging c3-pawn instead of inventing a motif.
Rc8: pin of c3 to the rook on the c-file is the right geometry.
